correctness.rationale: For every normalized-area-uniform nondegenerate triangle, barycentric coordinates obey the exact Dirichlet beta identity. The squared centroid distance is a quadratic in zero-sum barycentric deviations; coefficient-by-coefficient exact rational expansion proves all three formulas. Nonzero third elementary symmetric coefficient yields an invertible cubic, while positive roots and Heron strict area characterize feasible triangles. Two explicit noncongruent positive-area witnesses share the first two moments but differ at order six. The exact checker verifies the universal polynomial identities and 201 rational examples; no finite simulation stands in for the proof.

value.rationale: The natural one-point centroidal radius histogram is a rotation-invariant geometric measurement. This result gives a complete, sharp finite inverse classification: three lowest even moments suffice for every triangle (including repeated sides), while two, although already determining area, fail by an explicit positive-area family. This is a precise inverse-geometric information threshold, not arbitrary parameter enumeration. Finite-sample stability remains open.
